issues.legal_issue: The validity of a long-term lease of ghatwali land for a permitted purpose is governed by the special law on ghatwali lands rather than inconsistent requirements in the general law governing estates under the Court of Wards.
material_facts: The land was part of a ghatwali estate under the management of the Court of Wards.
An official executed a perpetual lease on behalf of the Court of Wards for the purpose of erecting dwelling houses, a purpose specified in the special law.
The lessee and successors remained in possession for about eighty years, and the lease’s validity was not challenged during that period.
issues.conclusion: The special law governed the lease, and its requirements were satisfied; the lease was valid and binding on future possessors.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 1 and 2 of the Bengal Ghatwali Lands Act, 1859 permit leases for specified purposes, including erecting dwelling houses, and provide for leases granted by the Court of Wards to bind future possessors. The special provisions prevail over inconsistent provisions in the general Court of Wards Act, 1870 under the principle generalia specialibus non derogant, as described in Maxwell on the Interpretation of Statutes. Under section 114, illustration (e), of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, an official act may be presumed regularly performed; the Court inferred that the official who executed the lease was authorized to act for the Court of Wards.

rule.if: lease_validity_dispute and ghatwali_estate_land and lease_for_dwelling_houses and purported_official_execution_for_ward_authority and prolonged_unquestioned_possession

predicates.lease_validity_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a lease of estate land is valid and binding on successors or future possessors.
predicates.ghatwali_estate_land: The leased land forms part of a ghatwali estate.
predicates.lease_for_dwelling_houses: The lease was granted for the purpose of erecting dwelling houses.
predicates.purported_official_execution_for_ward_au: An official executed the lease on behalf of the authority managing the estate.
predicates.prolonged_unquestioned_possession: The lessee or successors remained in possession for a prolonged period without a challenge to the lease’s validity.

issues.definition: When a validity dispute concerns ghatwali estate land leased for dwelling houses through an official acting for the managing authority, and possession continues for a prolonged period without challenge, the lease is valid and binding.

issues.legal_issue: Even if the general law governing estates under the Court of Wards applies, a perpetual lease granted by a district officer can be sustained where the required approval is presumed from the circumstances.
material_facts: The estate was under the management of the Court of Wards when the perpetual lease was granted.
The Deputy Commissioner, who was also the Collector, executed the lease on behalf of the Court of Wards.
The lease document showed that it was perpetual, possession continued for about eighty years, and the lease’s validity was not challenged on the ground that Board approval was lacking.
issues.conclusion: Even on the assumption that the general law applied, the lease was not void because the required approval of the Board of Revenue could be presumed to have been obtained.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 8, 9 and 13 of the Court of Wards Act, 1870, read together, empower the Court of Wards to manage estates and permit a Collector to perform management functions for property in the Collector’s district; a lease beyond the ordinary term is effective with the sanction of the Board of Revenue. Section 114, illustration (e), of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 permits the presumption that official acts were regularly performed. Given the official lease, its stated perpetual term, and the long period of unchallenged possession, the Court presumed that the Board’s sanction had been obtained.

rule.if: lease_validity_dispute and estate_under_ward_management and perpetual_lease and district_officer_executed_lease_for_managing_authority and prolonged_unquestioned_possession

predicates.lease_validity_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a lease of estate land is valid and binding on successors or future possessors.
predicates.estate_under_ward_management: The estate was under the management of a public estate-management authority when the lease was granted.
predicates.perpetual_lease: The lease was granted in perpetuity.
predicates.district_officer_executed_lease_for_mana: A district officer executed the lease on behalf of the authority managing the estate.
predicates.prolonged_unquestioned_possession: The lessee or successors remained in possession for a prolonged period without a challenge to the lease’s validity.

issues.definition: When a validity dispute concerns a perpetual lease made by a district officer for an estate-management authority and possession continues for a prolonged period without challenge, the lease is valid and binding.

issues.legal_issue: Title to land not included in a lease remains with the titleholder, and possession of waste land may be presumed to follow title where effective enjoyment is unavailable.
material_facts: The lower courts found that the disputed C Schedule land was not included in the lease.
The lower courts found that title to that land vested in the plaintiff.
The land was waste land for which there could be no effective enjoyment.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff’s title to the C Schedule land stood, and possession was presumed to follow that title.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the presumption that possession follows title, particularly where the land is waste and there can be no effective enjoyment. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this principle.

rule.if: recovery_suit and land_not_included_in_lease and claimant_title_established and waste_land_without_effective_enjoyment

predicates.recovery_suit: The proceeding seeks recovery of possession of disputed land.
predicates.land_not_included_in_lease: The disputed land was not part of the lease relied on by the opposing party.
predicates.claimant_title_established: The claimant’s title to the disputed land has been established.
predicates.waste_land_without_effective_enjoyment: The land is waste and does not permit effective enjoyment.

issues.definition: In a recovery suit, when land lies outside the opposing party’s lease, the claimant’s title is established, and the land is waste without effective enjoyment, possession is presumed to follow title.

issues.legal_issue: A new contention that the claimant lacked standing because the estate had vested in the government should not be entertained for the first time on appeal where it was not raised below and related proceedings concerning vesting were pending.
material_facts: The suit was filed after the estate had vested in the government, but the defendants did not contest the claimant’s standing on that ground in the trial court.
The State was later added as a party in the High Court but did not assert a claim to the suit property.
Proceedings concerning whether a related tenure had vested in the State were pending, and the appellant raised the standing contention for the first time before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to permit the appellant to raise the new contention and left the vesting question open.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to entertain a contention raised for the first time on appeal in the circumstances, including the failure to raise it below, the State’s failure to claim the property, and the related pending proceedings. The Court cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this procedural decision.

rule.if: civil_appeal and standing_objection_not_raised_below and government_did_not_claim_disputed_property and related_vesting_proceedings_pending

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter is a civil appeal.
predicates.standing_objection_not_raised_below: The objection that the claimant lacks standing was not raised in the proceedings below.
predicates.government_did_not_claim_disputed_proper: The government, although joined as a party, did not assert a claim to the disputed property.
predicates.related_vesting_proceedings_pending: Related proceedings concerning vesting of the relevant tenure in the government were pending.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal, when a standing objection was not raised below, the government did not claim the property, and related vesting proceedings remain pending, the new objection is not entertained and the vesting question is left open.
